premise.claim: Stateful selective scale-down is needed for node failures, machine relocation, and application migration... RBG supports ordinary stateful scale-down by reducing replicas. Stateless RoleInstanceSet has a specified-delete flow, but Stateful mode does not expose persistent ordinal retirement. (issue #499)
premise.patchedComponent: api/workloads ordinals + admission, RBG/RIS controllers, stateful RIS rollout engine, discovery
premise.evidence: base 4a0765f7 contains no excluded-ordinals/committed-skip handling outside keps/ and doc/ (results/premise-base.txt); the base commit is the KEP-docs-only PR #513. The feature gap named by issue #499 (still OPEN) is real.

findings.note: Documents current replace semantics: an invalid committed record causes validateCommittedMembership to drop ALL FailedScale conditions (any reason) and install InvalidCommittedOrdinals. If the authors scope the filter to the InvalidCommittedOrdinals reason (the proposed fix), this canary flips red and must be inverted to a contract test.

Documents current behavior: with committed members [0,2,4] (record '1,3') and maxSurge=1, surge lands on ordinal 5 even when the role exclusion input is '1,3,5' (surge allocation sees only the committed record, never E). If the authors make surge allocation consult the exclusion input, this canary flips red and must be inverted to a contract test.
